title: Two opposing cells in one loop
caption: Go round the loop: the 6 V cell is a rise, the 2 V cell (facing the other way) is a drop, and the resistance takes the rest. ΣEMF = ΣIR gives 6 − 2 = I × 4, so I = 1 A, driven by the 6 V cell. The 2 V cell has current forced through it backwards, so it is being charged.
alt: Circuit with a 6 volt cell and a 2 volt cell facing opposite ways in a single loop with a 4 ohm resistor; a current of 1 amp flows clockwise.
description: A single rectangular loop. On the top wire is a 6 V cell with its positive (long) plate on the right. On the bottom wire are a 4 ohm resistor and a 2 V cell whose positive plate is also on the right, so it pushes the other way round the loop.
Arrows on the side wires show the current flowing clockwise: down the right-hand side and up the left. The current is 1 A.
Because the current flows into the 2 V cell's positive terminal, that cell is being charged.
note: net EMF = 6 − 2 = 4 V;  I = 4 V ÷ 4 Ω = 1 A

review.notes: Approved in both rounds; caption now notes the 2 V cell is being charged.
